notes:
Sanctioned strength: the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026 (Cabinet approved 2026-05-05; raises the Court from 34 to 38, i.e. puisne judges from 33 to 37, excluding the CJI) passed Lok Sabha on 2026-08-03 and Rajya Sabha on 2026-08-05 (per PRS Legislative Research bill tracker). Presidential assent / gazette notification date could not be independently confirmed with the tools available (nja.gov.in and some gov.in domains were unreachable from this environment; PIB's press-release search was blocked by the site). The official sci.gov.in roster page, itself stamped 'Last Updated: Sep 25, 2026', lists exactly 34 sitting judges (CJI + 33) with no vacancies filled beyond that — so this file records 34 as the actual current bench and flags the +4 as a likely-enacted-but-unfilled sanctioned increase rather than asserting it as settled fact. 

Parent High Court for each judge is the High Court (or post, e.g. Chief Justice of X High Court) they held immediately before elevation to the Supreme Court, per each judge's official sci.gov.in biography — not necessarily the High Court where they were first appointed a judge, since many judges are transferred/elevated to become Chief Justice of a different High Court shortly before Supreme Court elevation. Three sitting judges (P.S. Narasimha, K.V. Viswanathan, V. Mohana) were elevated directly from the Bar and have no parent High Court. 

Could not independently confirm current holders/dates for: Supreme Court Legal Services Committee Chairman (sclsc.gov.in appears stale, footer copyright 2022) — no position invented, entity flagged confidence medium with an explanatory internal note; National Judicial Academy Director's currency (only a July 2026 Wayback snapshot available, live site unreachable). Wikipedia pages could not be located/confirmed for 3 of the 33 puisne judges (Sanjay Kumar, S.V.N. Bhatti, N.V. Anjaria) despite multiple title guesses — the Wikimedia API opensearch endpoint was rate-limited for most of this research session (heavy parallel use across the wider gov-graph project), so this is a gap, not a confirmed absence. Attorney General for India (in-pos-attorney-general) is referenced only, per the core-apex ownership rule, in one ex_officio relation into SCLSC. 

24 internal single-purpose Supreme Court committees (Finance Committee, Library Committee, PIL Committee, etc., from sci.gov.in/committees) were deliberately NOT modelled as separate entities/relations — out of scope for this segment's brief (Secretary General/Registry, SCLSC, NALSA, NJA, e-Committee only) and would have added ~70 low-value, purely-internal committee memberships without materially improving the citizen-facing graph.

entities.name: Supreme Court of India
entities.description: India's apex constitutional court and final court of appeal, with original, appellate, advisory and writ jurisdiction; exercises judicial review over legislative and executive action and is the ultimate interpreter of the Constitution.
entities.legalBasis: Constitution of India, Articles 124-147 (Part V, Chapter IV)

stats.note: 34 = sitting CJI + 33 puisne judges as listed on sci.gov.in on 2026-09-25 (site 'Last Updated' stamp same date). Statutory ceiling raised from 34 (1 CJI + 33) to 38 (1 CJI + 37) by the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, which passed Lok Sabha on 2026-08-03 and Rajya Sabha on 2026-08-05; presidential assent/gazette notification date not independently confirmed, so the extra 4 sanctioned seats are treated here as vacant/unfilled rather than assumed enacted with certainty.

entities.name: Collegium of the Supreme Court of India
entities.description: An extra-constitutional, judge-only body — the Chief Justice of India and the four next most senior Supreme Court judges — that recommends appointments and transfers of judges to the Supreme Court and High Courts. Evolved through the Second and Third Judges Cases (1993, 1998); the executive cannot appoint a judge outside a collegium recommendation, though it can return a name once for reconsideration.
entities.legalBasis: Judge-made law: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v Union of India (1993) and In re Special Reference 1 of 1998 (interpreting Article 124(2))

entities.name: Registry of the Supreme Court of India
entities.description: The administrative and case-management arm of the Supreme Court, headed by the Secretary General and staffed by Registrars and Registrars (Judicial) who handle filing, listing, court records and day-to-day administration.

entities.name: Supreme Court Legal Services Committee
entities.description: Provides free legal aid, advice and representation to eligible weaker-section litigants in cases before the Supreme Court, and runs Lok Adalats and mediation for such matters. Chaired by a sitting Supreme Court judge (nominated by the CJI) with nine CJI-nominated members; the Attorney General and the Secretary General of the Supreme Court are ex-officio members.

entities.name: National Legal Services Authority
entities.description: The apex statutory body constituted to provide free legal aid to weaker sections of society, organise Lok Adalats and promote access to justice nationwide; oversees the State/District Legal Services Authorities. The sitting CJI is ex-officio Patron-in-Chief; the senior-most sitting Supreme Court judge after the CJI is Executive Chairman.

entities.name: National Judicial Academy
entities.description: The apex judicial-training institution of India, on a 63-acre campus at Bhopal; trains judges and judicial officers and conducts research on judicial administration. Registered as a society in 1993; its Governing Council is chaired by the Chief Justice of India.
entities.legalBasis: Registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860

entities.name: e-Committee, Supreme Court of India
entities.description: Advises the Chief Justice of India on the national policy for information and communication technology (ICT) in the Indian judiciary, and plans/monitors the eCourts Mission Mode Project across all courts.
entities.legalBasis: Constituted by the Supreme Court of India (Government of India Resolution, 2004)

holder.name: Surya Kant
holder.notes: 53rd CJI. Born 1962-02-10 at Hisar, Haryana. Was Chief Justice of the Himachal Pradesh High Court (elevated to that post 2018-10-05) before elevation as a Supreme Court judge on 2019-05-24; earlier a permanent judge (2004) and Advocate General (2000) of Haryana at the Punjab & Haryana High Court. Due to retire 2027-02-09 (turns 65). Ex officio Patron-in-Chief of NALSA and SCLSC, and Patron-in-Chief of the e-Committee, and Chairperson of the National Judicial Academy Governing Council.
